description:
FOUND by the fz-kdt.127.2 adversarial refutation (F7).

WHAT. `callable_clauses` (src/compiler2/types/mod.rs) reports an ANONYMOUS
literal -- fz-kdt.127.2's `ClosureLit` with `fn_id: None` -- as
`closure: None`, which is the same thing it reports for a bare SURFACE clause
that pins no literal at all. `callable_value_clauses` then reads that as a
surface: it collects every `closure.is_none()` clause as a specializer and
`continue`s past it in the result loop:

    if clause.closure.is_none() { continue; }

So a union holding one anonymous literal beside one or more branded ones would
resolve, at `resolve_closure_call`, to the BRANDED targets only -- the "some
other brand, these capture types" member silently dropped, and the anonymous
clause additionally used to specialize the survivors' args/ret.

WHY IT IS NOT LIVE. An anonymous literal is minted in exactly one place,
`Types::erase_transported_closure_identities`, which puts it in the `arrow` of
the ACTIVATION KEY of a non-recursive body that consumes no callable identity,
and only in slots the dispatch mask marks `DispatchDemand::Ignore`; call
resolution reads a VALUE's type, never a key. The refuter instrumented the
anonymous arm of `callable_clauses` and measured 0 hits over 597 corpus
fixtures (with and without `--dump backend=`) and 1 hit over the whole
`cargo test --lib` -- that one being the conformance unit test that constructs
an erased literal directly.

WHAT IS MISSING is that nothing STATES or ENFORCES it at this site.
fz-kdt.127.2 put the statement and a `debug_assert!` gate on the dispatch-test
road (`callable_identity_targets`); the call-resolution road has neither, and
`closure: None` conflating "no literal" with "a literal with no brand" is the
kind of lookalike the fold-concordant-ideas rule warns about.

WORK: decide whether `CallableClause::closure` should distinguish the two
(an anonymous literal is NOT a surface -- it pins captures), or whether one
loud refusal in `callable_value_clauses` is the right shape; either way pin it
with a unit test that builds `erase(L3(int)) | L5(float)` and asserts the
result is not the branded clause alone. Note a plain `debug_assert!` in
`callable_clauses` is NOT cheap: the fz-kdt.127.2 conformance test
`erase_closure_identity_drops_the_brand_and_keeps_the_captures` calls it on an
erased literal on purpose.
title: An anonymous closure literal sharing a callable union with a branded one would be dropped by callable_value_clauses: unreachable today, unstated and unenforced
